_comment: Hourly prices for the things this project runs. This file is the single place
an hourly figure lives; nothing else in scripts/ or docs/ may carry one.
Rule 5 of the workspace rules: every number in the README, the wiki or a blog draft
traces to
a file under materials/, and no number is written from memory. That applies here
with force, because these figures are what `mise run up` prints to the human
immediately before it spends their money. A rate that is wrong by a factor of ten
and looks plausible is worse than no rate at all.
So every usd_per_hour below is null until someone has looked it up and written
down where and when. `mise run up` refuses to open a window while any of them is
null, and says which. Fill each one in with:
usd_per_hour  the number, in the currency and region named below
source_url    the AWS pricing page or Price List API query it came from
sourced_on    the date it was read, as YYYY-MM-DD
quantity and max_quantity are structural, not prices, so they are filled in
already. quantity is the steady state an open window sits at. max_quantity is the
ceiling the stack itself permits, and it is the one the confirmation prompt uses,
because the number the human is checking against the `max $<amount>` in their own
approval message has to be a ceiling and not a hope. Every max_quantity below is
traced to the variable in this repository that enforces it; if that variable moves,
this file moves with it.
Spot prices move. The GPU line is a Spot price and is therefore an estimate with
a shelf life; re-read it before each window rather than trusting last month's.
The authoritative reading for a specific hour is ec2 describe-spot-price-history
for the instance type and Availability Zone, which is a read-only call and is
allowed in LOCAL mode.
Not everything the project bills for is hourly. Data transfer, S3 requests, ECR
storage, CloudWatch Logs ingestion and NAT gateway data processing are per-unit
and are recorded in materials/costs/windows.md after the fact, not estimated here.
`mise run audit` reports the standing per-unit ones it can see so that they reach
the window record instead of nowhere.
There is deliberately no load balancer line. Every Service in this repository is
ClusterIP, no AWS Load Balancer Controller is installed, and nothing in any of the
three stacks creates an elastic load balancer, so pricing one would put a resource
in the estimate that cannot exist. If an ingress is ever added, the line comes back
with the same treatment as the rest: null until somebody reads the price.
--- How the figures below were read, 2026-09-10 ---
Everything except the Spot line comes from the AWS Price List Bulk API, which needs
no credentials. The entry point is
https://pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/offers/v1.0/aws/index.json, whose offers map
gives each service a currentRegionIndexUrl; that region index gives the us-east-1
currentVersionUrl. Each source_url below is the stable /current/us-east-1/index.json
alias for that service, which redirects to whatever the newest version is, so the URL
keeps working while the number under it moves. The exact versions read on 2026-09-10
The SKU behind each figure, so the reading can be repeated rather than trusted:
eks_control_plane    AmazonEKS ZYWMR684YSMFHWEU, usagetype USE1-AmazonEKS-Hours:perCluster,
tiertype HAStandard, unit Hours. That is the standard-support
cluster hour; the extended-support SKU is a different one
(M7977BSVFGDUJZ67) and this project never reaches it.
nat_gateway          AmazonEC2 M2YSHUBETB3JX4M4, productFamily NAT Gateway,
usagetype NatGateway-Hours, 'Hourly charge for NAT Gateways'.
The per-GB SKUs (NatGateway-Bytes, RegionalNatGateway-Bytes) are
the data processing charge and are deliberately not priced here.
public_ipv4_address  AmazonVPC 4GQUNXTFWVSGPUZK, usagetype USE1-PublicIPv4:InUseAddress.
The idle-address SKU is separate and does not apply while the
address is attached to a live NAT gateway.
system_node          AmazonEC2 NN4EGUUQRWVYP98C, BoxUsage:t3.medium, Linux, Shared
tenancy, preInstalledSw NA, capacitystatus Used, no license.
gp3 storage          AmazonEC2 JG3KUJMBRGHV3N8G, EBS:VolumeUsage.gp3, $0.08 per GB-month.
Both EBS lines below divide that by 730 hours per month, the
divisor the AWS Pricing Calculator uses, and multiply by the
volume size this repository provisions.
g6.xlarge on demand  AmazonEC2 TPKUC6XYSUQ3VFK2, BoxUsage:g6.xlarge, Linux, Shared
tenancy, no license. Used only as the ceiling under gpu_node; see
the note there.
The two instance figures were cross-checked against the Pricing Calculator feed at
https://b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/ec2/USD/current/ec2-ondemand-without-sec-sel/US%20East%20(N.%20Virginia)/Linux/index.json
which returns the same 0.0416 and 0.8048.

eks_control_plane.description: EKS control plane, one cluster, standard support

nat_gateway.description: NAT gateway, hourly charge only; data processing is per GB and is not estimated here

public_ipv4_address.description: In-use public IPv4 address hourly charge on the NAT gateway's Elastic IP. A separate hourly dimension from the NAT gateway itself
public_ipv4_address.ceiling_source: one Elastic IP, on the single NAT gateway in infra/cluster/vpc.tf

system_node.description: System managed node group, t3.medium on demand, carrying Karpenter, CoreDNS and monitoring

system_node_ebs.description: Root volume for each system node, gp3, converted from the per GB month price
system_node_ebs.ceiling_source: one volume per system node, so the same ceiling as system_node
system_node_ebs.note: Per volume, not per GiB. 40 GiB, the default of infra/cluster system_node_disk_size, times $0.08 per GB-month, divided by 730 hours per month: 40 * 0.08 / 730 = 0.004383561..., rounded to eight places. 730 is the divisor the AWS Pricing Calculator uses, and gpu_node_ebs uses the same one.

gpu_node.description: GPU node, g6.xlarge on Spot. On demand GPU is denied by the boundary and is never priced here
gpu_node.ceiling_source: infra/cluster/platform inference_max_replicas 2, whose own description is 'One replica per GPU node'; gpu_nodepool_cpu_limit 8 holds the pool to the same two g6.xlarge
gpu_node.note: PLACEHOLDER CEILING, NOT A SPOT PRICE. READ THE REAL ONE BEFORE THE NEXT WINDOW. 0.8048 is the g6.xlarge Linux ON DEMAND rate (AmazonEC2 SKU TPKUC6XYSUQ3VFK2, BoxUsage:g6.xlarge), and source_url points at the on demand feed accordingly. It stands here only because a Spot price for an instance type is never above the on demand price for that type in the same Availability Zone, so an estimate built on it overstates the bill and never understates it. Spot appears in no public pricing feed and could not be read when this file was filled in, because ec2 describe-spot-price-history needs credentials for a role that did not exist yet. Replace this with an actual reading: aws ec2 describe-spot-price-history --instance-types g6.xlarge --product-descriptions 'Linux/UNIX' --availability-zone <az> --max-items 10, which is read only and allowed in LOCAL mode, then set source_url to that command and sourced_on to the day it was run. Until that happens, treat every total this line feeds as an upper bound and not as an expectation.

gpu_node_ebs.description: Root volume for the GPU node, gp3, converted from the per GB month price
gpu_node_ebs.ceiling_source: one volume per GPU node, so the same ceiling as gpu_node
gpu_node_ebs.note: Per volume, not per GiB. 120 GiB, the default of infra/cluster/platform gpu_node_volume_size and also the volume_max_size_gib ceiling in the operator boundary, times $0.08 per GB-month, divided by the same 730 hours per month used for system_node_ebs: 120 * 0.08 / 730 = 0.013150684..., rounded to eight places.
